pharm: Synthetic oral serine protease inhibitor (camostat mesilate) that inhibits trypsin and related proteases; approved in Japan for chronic pancreatitis and postoperative reflux esophagitis.
quick: Pancreatitis: 600 mg/day in 3 divided doses; reflux: 300 mg/day in 3 divided doses
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; limited data
Symptoms, pancreatic enzymes, hypersensitivity, blood counts
summary: Camostat (camostat mesilate, Foipan) is an orally active synthetic serine protease inhibitor approved in Japan for relief of acute symptoms (acute exacerbations) of chronic pancreatitis and for postoperative reflux esophagitis. It inhibits trypsin and other proteases, reducing pancreatic autodigestion and inflammation. It is not FDA-approved; this record reflects the Japanese label and published literature. It has also been investigated (as a TMPRSS2 inhibitor) for COVID-19.
indications: Relief of acute symptoms (acute exacerbations) of chronic pancreatitis
Investigational: antiviral (TMPRSS2 inhibition, e.g., COVID-19) - not approved
admin: Take orally after meals, in three divided doses
Adjust dose for chronic pancreatitis according to symptom severity
Avoid alcohol and follow dietary advice for pancreatitis
Discontinue if hypersensitivity or significant adverse effects occur
moa: Camostat is a synthetic serine protease inhibitor that inhibits trypsin and other proteases (including kallikrein, plasmin, and the membrane serine protease TMPRSS2). In pancreatitis it suppresses excessive protease activity and pancreatic autodigestion/inflammation; protease inhibition also underlies its investigational antiviral effect by blocking viral spike-protein priming.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to camostat mesilate or product components

preg: Use only if the potential benefit outweighs the risk; human safety data in pregnancy are limited.
lact: Avoid or use with caution during breastfeeding; data on excretion in milk are limited.
renal: No established dose adjustment; limited data. Use with caution in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution; rare hepatic enzyme elevation has been reported. Limited data on dose adjustment.

moderate: Theoretical interaction with other agents affecting protease/coagulation pathways
minor: No clinically significant interactions well established in the literature
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol, which can worsen pancreatitis

monitoring: Symptom response (abdominal pain in pancreatitis; reflux symptoms)
Complete blood count in prolonged therapy (rare cytopenias)
counsel: Take after each meal, three times a day, as directed
Avoid alcohol and follow your recommended diet for pancreatitis
Report any rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing
Tell your doctor about any history of drug allergies or blood disorders
This medicine is approved in some countries (e.g., Japan) and is not FDA-approved
pk: Rapidly hydrolyzed after oral absorption to active metabolite (GBPA/FOY-251)
Short (parent rapidly metabolized; active metabolite ~1 hour)
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture per label
pearls: NOTE: Approved in Japan (Foipan) and not FDA-approved - this record reflects the Japanese label and published literature
Oral serine protease inhibitor used for chronic pancreatitis flares and postoperative reflux esophagitis
Rapidly metabolized to active metabolite GBPA (FOY-251)
Inhibits TMPRSS2, prompting investigation as an antiviral (e.g., COVID-19) - not an approved indication
Generally well tolerated; watch for rare hypersensitivity and blood/liver abnormalities
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. Resume the regular three-times-daily schedule.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; expect exaggerated GI effects and possible hypersensitivity. Manage supportively and discontinue the drug; monitor blood counts and hepatic function.
